page.layout: Top: two circular portrait medallions with engraved inscriptions, left and right. Below them one column of running text, two paragraphs. No notes in the margins. Running head at top, page number at top left.

main_text.p: CHRISTOPHORVS Longolius Parisiensis,suo tem-pore,eloquetia magna prestitit, vtpote qui plures scripserit Latinè elegantissimas orationes, Epistolas,Epigrámata, & Elegias. Porro inter orationes,vnā exarauit in laudem Ludouici Regis, vndecimi,alteram in laudem Plinij , quinquealias in laudé vr-bis Romę,& vnā aduersus Lutheranos. Scripsit etiā amicis plu-res Epistolas,vt Erasmo,Budęo, Bembo, Sadoleto & aliis. Scri-psit quoque in Ius ciuile,cū publicè Iurisprudentiā profiteretur in Academia Piętonū. Erat valde comis & humanus,vnde om-niū amicitiā sibi cōparabat. Sed cū videamus sepissimè chario-res & virtutibus ornatiores potius quā vitiosos immatura ætate è viuis excedere , florentibus adhuc annis,vitā cū morte muta-uit,cū trigētisimū sextū suę ætatis annū nōdū attigisset. Omnia eius opera fuerūt impressa Lugduni, à Sebastiano Gryphio,& in pluribus locis Germanię & Italię.Florebat circiter annū 1536. Vide Conradum Gesnerum, in sua Bibliotheca.

ORONTIVS Fineus Delphinas Regius Mathematicarū profeßor,in oppido Briansonio natus,patre medico & Philosopho egregio,nec non Mathematico nobili: quo mortuo,Lutetiā venit, vbi perfectis iā suis studiis, vxorē duxit Dionysiā cognomine & re candidā,cū qua vixit paulò minus viginti annis. Quantū laboris insumpserit assiduis cōmentationibus, testantur tot eius scripta, quorū serie reperies in Bibliothec.Gesneri. Floruit anno salutis 1545. Et obiit Lutetię in suis ędibus pridie nonas Octobris,anno reparatę salutis hominū 1555. hora à meridie quarta, qua ille in lucem venerat, natus annos LXI. ferè: iacet in cœnobio Carmelitarum.

page.notes: The two medallion inscriptions are engraved in the illustrations and are given as lines. "ORONTIVS FINAEI." reads from the right medallion; the word order on the right side is not fully certain. Long s has been normalised to plain s. The scan is clear enough to read all printed lines.
